1+;; wasm.arrays — P3.1: let-go's mutable typed arrays as the runtime sees them
2+;; (int-array, byte-array, aget, aset, alength, aclone, bytes), in the
3+;; runtime dialect of seq.lg (IR special forms, IR-op core fns on :int,
4+;; wasm.intrinsics, and the runtime namespaces it requires). Ground truth is
5+;; let-go 4e769212: pkg/vm/typed_array.go (TypedArray, TypedArraySeq) and
6+;; pkg/rt/lang.go (buildArray :5046, CoreAgetf :9036, CoreAsetf :9074,
7+;; CoreAlengthf :9098, CoreAclonef :9111, CoreBytesf :9124).
8+;;
9+;; An array is `Arr`: element kind (0 byte, 1 int: ArrayByte/ArrayInt) and
10+;; the backing wasm array (wasm/Bytes, or I64s), mutable in place and never
11+;; resized. Only the two kinds xsofy builds exist; double-array and
12+;; object-array (and conj/empty, which make an object-array) are named
13+;; limits. Loaded before wasm.core, which refines kind 18 to 37 for an Arr
14+;; and routes type/count/seq/print/get/nth here; the messages that name an
15+;; argument's type ("aget expects array, got let-go.lang.Int") need
16+;; wasm.core's type-name, which this namespace reaches through the hook
17+;; wasm.core/install! sets (it cannot require wasm.core: wasm.core requires
18+;; it).
19+;;
20+;; Calling convention as seq.lg (D37); errors raise the backend's exception
21+;; value as wasm.core does (D68), msg = cmsg (natives called as values).
22+(ns wasm.arrays
23+ (:refer-clojure :exclude [aget aset alength aclone bytes int-array byte-array])
24+ (:require [wasm.intrinsics :as wasm]
25+ [wasm.pvec :as pv]
26+ [wasm.seq :as sq]
27+ [wasm.str :as s]))
28+
29+(wasm/defarray I64s :i64)
30+(wasm/defstruct Arr [:i32 :ref]) ; element kind 0 byte / 1 int, backing array
31+;; The one runtime global (D39): the Fn (f x) -> Str giving a value's type
32+;; name, set by wasm.core/install!.
33+(wasm/defstruct AGlobals [[:mut :ref]])
34+(def globals (wasm/new AGlobals (wasm/null)))
35+
36+(defn set-type-name-hook! [f] (wasm/set! AGlobals 0 globals f))
37+
38+(defn arr? [x] (if (wasm/null? x) false (wasm/is? Arr x)))
39+(defn akind [a] (wasm/get Arr 0 a))
40+(defn adata [a] (wasm/get Arr 1 a))
41+(defn alen* [a] (wasm/alen (adata a)))
42+(defn aget* "Element i of Arr a as a boxed Int (TypedArray.Get)." [a i]
43+ (if (= 0 (akind a)) (sq/box-int (wasm/bget (adata a) i)) (sq/box-int (wasm/aget I64s (adata a) i))))
44+

46+(defn- raise [bs] (throw (wasm/new sq/Err 1 bs bs (wasm/null) (wasm/null))))
47+(defn- raise-str [st] (raise (s/str-bytes st)))
48+(defn- tn [x] (sq/invoke1 (wasm/get AGlobals 0 globals) x))
49+(defn- raise-arity [n] (raise-str (s/str (lit (wasm/bytes-of-string "wrong number of arguments ")) (sq/box-int n))))
50+(defn- raise-got [prefix x] (raise-str (s/str (lit prefix) (tn x))))

53+;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
54+;; Construction (buildArray)

58+;; TypedArray.Set: a byte element keeps the low 8 bits (byte(n)).
59+(defn- set-elem! [a i v]
60+ (if (int-val? v)
61+ (if (= 0 (akind a))
62+ (wasm/bset! (adata a) i (sq/unbox-int v))
63+ (wasm/aset! I64s (adata a) i (sq/unbox-int v)))
64+ (raise-got (if (= 0 (akind a)) (wasm/bytes-of-string "byte-array expects Int, got ")
65+ (wasm/bytes-of-string "int-array expects Int, got "))
66+ v)))

68+(defn- build-sized [k n init fill?]
69+ (if (< n 0)
70+ (raise-str (s/str (lit (wasm/bytes-of-string "negative array size: ")) (sq/box-int n)))
71+ (let [a (new-arr k n)]
72+ (when fill? (loop [i 0] (when (< i n) (set-elem! a i init) (recur (inc i)))))
73+ a)))

76+ (let [v (if (= 11 (sq/kind coll))
77+ coll

79+ n (pv/vcount v)
80+ a (new-arr k n)]
81+ (loop [i 0]
82+ (if (< i n)
83+ (let [x (pv/vnth v i)]
84+ (if (int-val? x)
85+ (if (= k 0) (wasm/bset! (adata a) i (sq/unbox-int x)) (wasm/aset! I64s (adata a) i (sq/unbox-int x)))

94+(defn- scalar-kind? [k]

99+ (scalar-kind? (sq/kind x)) (raise-got (wasm/bytes-of-string "don't know how to create ISeq from ") x)
100+ :else (build-seq k x)))

102+(defn ^{:twin "core/int-array"} int-array
103+ ([] (raise-arity 0))
104+ ([x] (build 1 x (wasm/null) false))

108+(defn ^{:twin "core/byte-array"} byte-array
109+ ([] (raise-arity 0))
110+ ([x] (build 0 x (wasm/null) false))

117+(defn- checked-index [a idx] ; the index checks aget and aset share
118+ (if (int-val? idx)
119+ (let [i (sq/unbox-int idx) n (alen* a)]
120+ (if (if (< i 0) true (>= i n))

124+ -1))

137+ ([] (raise-arity 0))

154+(defn ^{:twin "core/alength"} alength
155+ ([] (raise-arity 0))
156+ ([a] (if (arr? a) (sq/box-int (alen* a)) (raise-got (wasm/bytes-of-string "alength expects array, got ") a)))
157+ ([a b] (raise-arity 2)))

160+ ([] (raise-arity 0))
161+ ([a] (if (arr? a)
162+ (let [n (alen* a) b (new-arr (akind a) n)]
163+ (if (= 0 (akind a))
164+ (wasm/array-copy wasm/Bytes (adata b) 0 (adata a) 0 n)
165+ (wasm/array-copy I64s (adata b) 0 (adata a) 0 n))

1+;; wasm.core — P2.7 runtime half: the generic collection dispatchers, the
2+;; numeric natives as values, state (atom, volatile), metadata, exceptions,
3+;; and the remaining shared natives, in the runtime dialect of seq.lg (IR
4+;; special forms, IR-op core fns on :int and :float, macros expanding to
5+;; those, wasm.intrinsics, and the other runtime namespaces). Loaded last: it
6+;; is the one namespace that sees every collection, so the dispatchers that
7+;; must tell a map from a set from a vector live here. Ground truth is
8+;; let-go 4e769212 (pkg/rt/lang.go, native_prims.go, builtins/builtins.go,
9+;; pkg/vm/numbers.go, transient.go, atom.go, persistent_map.go).
10+;;
11+;; Calling convention as seq.lg (D37): natives take and return refs; ints
12+;; arrive boxed, booleans leave as sq/Bool refs. Variadic natives get fixed
13+;; arities 0-4 (D52's ceiling) plus a `-seq` form taking the argument list.
14+;;
15+;; Errors let-go raises as catchable Go errors are raised here as the
16+;; backend's exception value: `(throw (wasm/new sq/Err 1 msg cmsg nil nil))`,
17+;; kind 1, msg the uncaught `error: ` text and cmsg what ex-message returns
18+;; once caught. A native called as a value reports its error unprefixed
19+;; either way ((def f +) (f Long/MAX 1) => "integer overflow"), so msg = cmsg;
20+;; the IR-op path's "ExecutionError: " prefix belongs to the backend (D16).
21+;; `throw` is the one core fn referenced: the backend lowers #'throw to the
22+;; wasm `throw $lgex` instruction (D25, D31). Internal invariants stay
23+;; wasm/trap. Named limits (Phase 3+ work) are wasm/trap with a
24+;; "lower-wasm: " message.
25+(ns wasm.core
26+ (:refer-clojure :exclude [assoc dissoc get contains? conj nth peek pop transient persistent! conj! assoc! dissoc!
27+ key val subvec complement max min mod number? map? set? seq? sorted? vector?
28+ list? fn? nil? string? keyword? symbol? coll? sequential? atom deref reset! swap!
29+ compare-and-set! volatile! vreset! vswap! with-meta meta gensym apply* bound-fn*
30+ ex-info ex-data ex-message ex-cause sort read-string slurp open compare])
31+ (:require [wasm.intrinsics :as wasm]
32+ [wasm.pvec :as pv]
33+ [wasm.seq :as sq]
34+ [wasm.str :as s]
35+ [wasm.phm :as m]
36+ [wasm.phs :as hs]
37+ [wasm.arrays :as arr]))

41+;; its count/equiv/hash through the generic hook slot (2) installed below.

44+(wasm/defstruct TypeVal [:ref :i64]) ; a let-go ValueType: name bytes, id (interned)

197+(defn invoke-args

207+ (= n 2) (sq/invoke2 f a b)

229+(defn- add2 [a b] ; NumAdd

231+ (cond (if (= ka 1) (= kb 1) false)
232+ (let [x (sq/unbox-int a) y (sq/unbox-int b) r (wasm/i64-add x y)]
233+ (if (< (bit-and (bit-xor x r) (bit-xor y r)) 0) (overflow) (sq/box-int r)))
234+ (if (num-k? ka) (num-k? kb) false) (s/box-float (+ (f64-of a ka) (f64-of b kb)))
235+ :else (raise-two (lit (wasm/bytes-of-string "cannot add ")) a b))))

241+ (if (< (bit-and (bit-xor x y) (bit-xor x r)) 0) (overflow) (sq/box-int r)))
242+ (if (num-k? ka) (num-k? kb) false) (s/box-float (- (f64-of a ka) (f64-of b kb)))

249+ (> a 0) (cond (if (> b 0) (> a (quot 9223372036854775807 b)) false) false
250+ (if (< b 0) (< b (quot -9223372036854775808 a)) false) false
251+ :else true)
252+ :else (cond (if (> b 0) (< a (quot -9223372036854775808 b)) false) false
253+ (if (< b 0) (< a (quot 9223372036854775807 b)) false) false

273+ (recur (cond (= op 0) (add2 acc (sq/first s)) (= op 1) (sub2 acc (sq/first s)) :else (mul2 acc (sq/first s)))

530+(defn get-nf

846+;; Metadata (CoreWithMeta, lang.go:7898). Vectors, maps and sets carry it in
847+;; a field (assoc/conj/disj/pop keep it); a list in its head cell (conj keeps
848+;; it, rest does not); a fn by wrapping (vm.NewMetaFn): a new Fn whose code
849+;; refs forward to the inner fn through a MetaEnv env, which no closure the
850+;; backend builds can have, so `meta` recognises it. Everything else is
851+;; returned unchanged, as native does for a MapEntry, a seq or a scalar.
852+
853+(defn- meta-inner [self] (wasm/get MetaEnv 0 (wasm/get sq/Fn 3 self)))
854+(defn- mfn0 [self] (sq/invoke0 (meta-inner self)))
855+(defn- mfn1 [self a] (sq/invoke1 (meta-inner self) a))
856+(defn- mfn2 [self a b] (sq/invoke2 (meta-inner self) a b))
857+(defn- mfn3 [self a b c] (invoke3 (meta-inner self) a b c))
858+(defn- mfn4 [self a b c d] (invoke4 (meta-inner self) a b c d))
859+
860+(defn- meta-fn? [f] (wasm/is? MetaEnv (wasm/get sq/Fn 3 f)))
861+
862+(defn- fn-with-meta [f mt]
863+ ;; wrap the innermost fn: (with-meta (with-meta f a) b) replaces a
864+ (let [g (if (meta-fn? f) (meta-inner f) f)]
865+ (wasm/new sq/Fn
866+ (if (wasm/null? (wasm/get sq/Fn 0 g)) (wasm/null) (wasm/funcref sq/Code0 mfn0))
867+ (if (wasm/null? (wasm/get sq/Fn 1 g)) (wasm/null) (wasm/funcref sq/Code1 mfn1))
868+ (if (wasm/null? (wasm/get sq/Fn 2 g)) (wasm/null) (wasm/funcref sq/Code2 mfn2))
869+ (wasm/new MetaEnv g mt)
870+ (if (wasm/null? (wasm/get sq/Fn 4 g)) (wasm/null) (wasm/funcref sq/Code3 mfn3))
871+ (if (wasm/null? (wasm/get sq/Fn 5 g)) (wasm/null) (wasm/funcref sq/Code4 mfn4))
872+ (wasm/get sq/Fn 6 g))))

877+ (= k 11) (pv/vwith-meta x mt)

1+;; wasm.host — P3.1: the natives xsofy reaches that talk to the outside:
2+;; printing (println print pr prn), IO handles (write! flush! close!), the
3+;; clocks (System/nanoTime, System/currentTimeMillis), sleeping through a
4+;; timeout channel (async/timeout, async/<!!), the browser seam (js/emit,
5+;; js/url-param), and let-go.core/now as a named limit. In the runtime
6+;; dialect of seq.lg; everything leaves through wasm/host-write,
7+;; wasm/host-sleep and wasm/host-nanotime (D6, D27: deterministic virtual
8+;; clock in the reference).
9+;;
10+;; Ground truth is let-go 4e769212: pkg/rt/lang.go (println :3670, print
11+;; :3652, pr :3661, prn :3300; text from prThroughToString,
12+;; print_method.go:12: the args' print-str/pr-str forms joined by one
13+;; space), pkg/rt/iort.go (close! :203, write! :260, flush! :282, *out*
14+;; and *err* :356), pkg/rt/system.go:148-155, pkg/rt/async.go (timeout,
15+;; <!! = <!), pkg/rt/js.go:66-100.
16+;;
17+;; *out*/*err* are values, not natives: `out-handle`/`err-handle` return
18+;; the runtime's two handles (fd 1, fd 2), which the backend binds those
19+;; vars to. Natively *out* is rebindable (with-out-str); here printing
20+;; always goes to fd 1, and the reference's host-write prints to the lg
21+;; *out*, so with-out-str still captures it in tests. Channels: only the
22+;; timeout channel exists (xsofy sleeps with (<!! (timeout ms))); chan, go
23+;; and >! are Phase 5.
24+(ns wasm.host
25+ (:refer-clojure :exclude [println print pr prn write! flush! close!])
26+ (:require [wasm.intrinsics :as wasm]
27+ [wasm.seq :as sq]
28+ [wasm.str :as s]
29+ [wasm.core :as c]
30+ [wasm.arrays :as arr]))

32+(wasm/defstruct Handle [:i64 :ref [:mut :i32]]) ; fd, name bytes (/dev/stdout), closed (1/0)
33+(wasm/defstruct Chan [:i64 [:mut :i32]]) ; a timeout: deadline (host ns), closed (1/0)
34+;; The one runtime global (D39): the two standard handles.
35+(wasm/defstruct HGlobals [:ref :ref])
36+(def globals (wasm/new HGlobals (wasm/new Handle 1 (wasm/bytes-of-string "/dev/stdout") 0)
37+ (wasm/new Handle 2 (wasm/bytes-of-string "/dev/stderr") 0)))

39+(defn out-handle "The value of *out*." [] (wasm/get HGlobals 0 globals))
40+(defn err-handle "The value of *err*." [] (wasm/get HGlobals 1 globals))

114+;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
115+;; Clocks. The host's clock (virtual in the reference, D27): nanoTime is it
116+;; directly; currentTimeMillis is it in ms (native: Unix epoch ms, so only
117+;; differences are comparable).
118+
119+(defn ^{:twin "System/nanoTime"} nano-time [] (sq/box-int (wasm/host-nanotime)))
120+(defn ^{:twin "System/currentTimeMillis"} current-time-millis [] (sq/box-int (quot (wasm/host-nanotime) 1000000)))
121+(defn ^{:twin "let-go.core/now"} now []
122+ (wasm/trap "lower-wasm: let-go.core/now returns a Go time.Time (host interop; `time` needs .Sub)"))
123+
124+;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
125+;; Timeout channels. (timeout ms) fixes a deadline now; the first take
126+;; sleeps until it (time.After fires once), later takes return at once.
127+;; A negative ms fires immediately.
128+
129+(defn ^{:twin "async/timeout"} timeout
130+ ([] (raise-arity 0))
131+ ([ms] (if (= 1 (sq/kind ms))
132+ (let [n (sq/unbox-int ms)] (wasm/new Chan (+ (wasm/host-nanotime) (if (< n 0) 0 (* n 1000000))) 0))
133+ (c/raise (wasm/bytes-of-string "timeout expected Int milliseconds"))))
134+ ([ms x] (raise-arity 2)))
135+
136+(defn ^{:twin "async/<!!"} take!!
137+ ([] (raise-arity 0))
138+ ([ch] (if (chan? ch)
139+ (do (when (= 0 (wasm/get Chan 1 ch))
140+ (let [wait (- (wasm/get Chan 0 ch) (wasm/host-nanotime))]
141+ (when (> wait 0) (wasm/host-sleep (quot (+ wait 999999) 1000000))))
142+ (wasm/set! Chan 1 ch 1))
143+ (wasm/null))
144+ (c/raise (wasm/bytes-of-string "<! expected Chan"))))
145+ ([ch x] (raise-arity 2)))
146+
147+;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
148+;; The browser seam (D100). emit validates its arguments, marshals data to
149+;; JSON exactly as let-go does (prepareEmit, pkg/rt/js.go: fromValue,
150+;; pkg/rt/json.go:103, then encoding/json.Marshal) and hands both to the host
151+;; through wasm/host-emit; url-param reads the page's query through
152+;; wasm/host-url-param. Their references are native lg off the browser: the
153+;; event goes nowhere and every parameter is absent (nil), so the oracle
154+;; still holds; a browser host (host/lg-wasm-host.js) fires the CustomEvent
155+;; and answers ?seed= and friends.
156+
157+(defn ^{:intrinsic true
158+ :wasm "copy name and JSON Bytes to linear memory at 32; call $env.emit(name_ptr, name_len, json_ptr, json_len)"
159+ :type "[:any :any] -> :any"}
160+ host-emit
161+ "Hand an event name and its JSON text (both Bytes) to the host."
162+ [name-bytes json-bytes] nil)
163+
164+(defn ^{:intrinsic true
165+ :wasm "copy name to 32; call $env.url_param(name_ptr, name_len, buf, cap) (getenv's contract); -1 -> ref.null, else Bytes"
166+ :type "[:any] -> :any"}
167+ host-url-param
168+ "The page URL's query parameter (Bytes name) as Bytes, or null when absent."
169+ [name-bytes] nil)
170+
171+;; A growable byte buffer for the JSON text: bytes, length.
172+(wasm/defstruct JBuf [[:mut :ref] [:mut :i64]])
173+(defn- jb-new [] (wasm/new JBuf (wasm/bytes-new 64) 0))
174+(defn- jb-room! [b extra]
175+ (let [bs (wasm/get JBuf 0 b) len (wasm/get JBuf 1 b) need (+ len extra)]
176+ (when (> need (wasm/alen bs))
177+ (let [nb (wasm/bytes-new (+ need need))]
178+ (wasm/array-copy wasm/Bytes nb 0 bs 0 len)
179+ (wasm/set! JBuf 0 b nb)))))
180+(defn- jb-byte! [b v]
181+ (jb-room! b 1)
182+ (wasm/bset! (wasm/get JBuf 0 b) (wasm/get JBuf 1 b) v)
183+ (wasm/set! JBuf 1 b (inc (wasm/get JBuf 1 b))))
184+(defn- jb-range! [b src from to]
185+ (let [n (- to from)]
186+ (jb-room! b n)
187+ (wasm/array-copy wasm/Bytes (wasm/get JBuf 0 b) (wasm/get JBuf 1 b) src from n)
188+ (wasm/set! JBuf 1 b (+ (wasm/get JBuf 1 b) n))))
189+(defn- jb-lit! [b bs] (jb-range! b bs 0 (wasm/alen bs)))
190+(defn- jb-done [b]
191+ (let [n (wasm/get JBuf 1 b) out (wasm/bytes-new n)]
192+ (wasm/array-copy wasm/Bytes out 0 (wasm/get JBuf 0 b) 0 n)
193+ out))
194+
195+(defn- hex-digit [d] (if (< d 10) (+ 48 d) (+ 87 d)))
196+
197+;; A JSON string as encoding/json writes it (encode.go appendString,
198+;; escapeHTML on): " \ and \n \r \t escaped, other bytes < 0x20 and < > & as
199+;; \u00XX, U+2028/U+2029 (E2 80 A8/A9) as  / , the rest verbatim.
200+;; (Go also replaces invalid UTF-8 with U+FFFD; the runtime's strings are
201+;; valid UTF-8 from source text and the host.)
202+(defn- json-string! [b bs]
203+ (jb-byte! b 34)
204+ (let [n (wasm/alen bs)]
205+ (loop [i 0 run 0]
206+ (if (>= i n)
207+ (jb-range! b bs run n)
208+ (let [c (wasm/bget bs i)
209+ ls? (if (= c 226) (if (< (+ i 2) n) (if (= 128 (wasm/bget bs (inc i)))
210+ (let [c3 (wasm/bget bs (+ i 2))] (if (= c3 168) true (= c3 169)))
211+ false) false) false)]
212+ (cond
213+ ls? (do (jb-range! b bs run i)
214+ (jb-lit! b (if (= 168 (wasm/bget bs (+ i 2))) (wasm/bytes-of-string "\\u2028") (wasm/bytes-of-string "\\u2029")))
215+ (recur (+ i 3) (+ i 3)))
216+ (if (< c 32) true (if (= c 34) true (if (= c 92) true (if (= c 60) true (if (= c 62) true (= c 38))))))
217+ (do (jb-range! b bs run i)
218+ (cond (= c 34) (jb-lit! b (wasm/bytes-of-string "\\\""))
219+ (= c 92) (jb-lit! b (wasm/bytes-of-string "\\\\"))
220+ (= c 10) (jb-lit! b (wasm/bytes-of-string "\\n"))
221+ (= c 13) (jb-lit! b (wasm/bytes-of-string "\\r"))
222+ (= c 9) (jb-lit! b (wasm/bytes-of-string "\\t"))
223+ :else (do (jb-lit! b (wasm/bytes-of-string "\\u00"))
224+ (jb-byte! b (hex-digit (quot c 16)))
225+ (jb-byte! b (hex-digit (bit-and c 15)))))
226+ (recur (inc i) (inc i)))
227+ :else (recur (inc i) run))))))
228+ (jb-byte! b 34))
229+
230+(defn- named-text
231+ "A keyword's Go string (ns/name, no colon), as fromValue reads it."
232+ [x] (let [bs (s/str-bytes (s/value-string x)) n (wasm/alen bs) out (wasm/bytes-new (- n 1))]
233+ (wasm/array-copy wasm/Bytes out 0 bs 1 (- n 1))
234+ out))
235+
236+(defn- json-key-str
237+ "A map key as fromMapValue (pkg/rt/json.go:58) names it, as a Str."
238+ [k] (let [kd (sq/kind k)]
239+ (cond (= kd 17) k
240+ (= kd 20) (s/mk-str (named-text k))
241+ :else (s/value-string k))))
242+
243+(declare json!)
244+
245+(defn- json-seq! [b xs]
246+ (jb-byte! b 91)
247+ (loop [s (sq/seq xs) first? true]
248+ (when-not (wasm/null? s)
249+ (when-not first? (jb-byte! b 44))
250+ (json! b (sq/first s))
251+ (recur (sq/next s) false)))
252+ (jb-byte! b 93))
253+
254+;; Go marshals map[string]any with its keys sorted, and a later entry whose
255+;; key converts to the same string replaces an earlier one: re-key into a
256+;; map by the converted Str, then walk its keys in sorted order.
257+(defn- json-map! [b m]
258+ (let [km (loop [s (sq/seq m) acc (wasm/null)]
259+ (if (wasm/null? s)
260+ acc
261+ (let [e (sq/first s)]
262+ (recur (sq/next s) (c/assoc acc (json-key-str (c/key e)) (c/val e))))))]
263+ (jb-byte! b 123)
264+ (loop [s (sq/seq (c/sort (loop [s (sq/seq km) ks (wasm/null)]
265+ (if (wasm/null? s) ks (recur (sq/next s) (sq/cons (c/key (sq/first s)) ks))))))
266+ first? true]
267+ (when-not (wasm/null? s)
268+ (let [k (sq/first s)]
269+ (when-not first? (jb-byte! b 44))
270+ (json-string! b (s/str-bytes k))
271+ (jb-byte! b 58)
272+ (json! b (c/get km k))
273+ (recur (sq/next s) false))))
274+ (jb-byte! b 125)))
275+
276+;; fromValue's cases: String, Int, Float (strconv 'f', -1 for |x| < 1e21:
277+;; a whole value prints with no fraction; elsewhere the runtime's float text,
278+;; which agrees on xsofy's payloads), Boolean, nil, maps (and records),
279+;; Keyword (its ns/name text), vectors and anything seqable as arrays, any
280+;; other value as its String().
281+(defn json! [b x]
282+ (let [k (sq/kind x) ck (c/ckind x)]
283+ (cond (= k 0) (jb-lit! b (wasm/bytes-of-string "null"))
284+ (= k 1) (jb-lit! b (s/str-bytes (s/value-string x)))
285+ (= k 15) (jb-lit! b (if (= 1 (wasm/get sq/Bool 0 x)) (wasm/bytes-of-string "true") (wasm/bytes-of-string "false")))
286+ (= k 17) (json-string! b (s/str-bytes x))
287+ (= k 20) (json-string! b (named-text x))
288+ (= k 22) (let [f (s/unbox-float x)]
289+ (if (if (< f 1.0e18) (if (> f -1.0e18) (= f (wasm/i64-to-f64 (wasm/f64-to-i64 f))) false) false)
290+ (jb-lit! b (s/str-bytes (s/value-string (sq/box-int (wasm/f64-to-i64 f)))))
291+ (jb-lit! b (s/str-bytes (s/value-string x)))))
292+ (= ck 30) (json-map! b x)
293+ (if (= k 11) true (if (sq/seq-kind? k) true (if (= ck 31) true (= k 23)))) (json-seq! b x)
294+ :else (json-string! b (s/str-bytes (s/value-string x))))))
295+
296+(defn json-bytes "data as the JSON text js/emit hands the host." [x]
297+ (let [b (jb-new)] (json! b x) (jb-done b)))
298+
299+(defn ^{:twin "js/emit"} emit
300+ ([] (c/raise (wasm/bytes-of-string "js/emit expects 2 args (event-name data), got 0")))
301+ ([a] (c/raise (wasm/bytes-of-string "js/emit expects 2 args (event-name data), got 1")))
302+ ([nm data] (let [k (sq/kind nm)]
303+ (cond (= k 20) (host-emit (named-text nm) (json-bytes data))
304+ (= k 21) (host-emit (s/str-bytes (s/value-string nm)) (json-bytes data))
305+ (= k 17) (host-emit (s/str-bytes nm) (json-bytes data))
306+ :else (raise-str (s/str (lit (wasm/bytes-of-string "js/emit event-name must be keyword, symbol, or string; got ")) (tn nm))))
307+ (wasm/null)))
308+ ([a b x] (c/raise (wasm/bytes-of-string "js/emit expects 2 args (event-name data), got 3"))))
309+
310+;; nil unless called with exactly one String (js.go: len(vs) != 1 or a
311+;; non-String name reads as absent).
312+(defn ^{:twin "js/url-param"} url-param
313+ ([] (wasm/null))
314+ ([nm] (if (= 17 (sq/kind nm))
315+ (let [bs (host-url-param (s/str-bytes nm))] (if (wasm/null? bs) (wasm/null) (s/mk-str bs)))
316+ (wasm/null)))
317+ ([nm x] (wasm/null)))

@@ -0,0 +1,522 @@
1+;; wasm.intrinsics — the intrinsic var set the wasm runtime is written
2+;; against (plan D4), plus its reference implementation under native lg.
3+;;
4+;; Every public defn tagged ^:intrinsic is recognised by the backend by var
5+;; identity at a :call site and emitted inline; its metadata names the wasm
6+;; instruction(s) (:wasm) and the typeinfer signature (:type). In the type
7+;; strings :int is i64, :float f64, :bool i32, :any (ref null eq). Indices and
8+;; lengths are :int on the lg side; the backend wraps them with i32.wrap_i64
9+;; and extends i32 results back with i64.extend_i32_s/u as noted.
10+;;
11+;; The reference implementation is deliberately stricter than wasm where
12+;; wasm would silently do something a correct runtime never relies on
13+;; (an out-of-range i31, an index >= 2^32 that wasm would wrap, a raw lg value
14+;; in a :ref slot): those throw here, so runtime bugs surface under native lg
15+;; before the backend exists. Where wasm has defined semantics that runtime
16+;; code DOES rely on (wrapping i64 arithmetic, shift counts mod 64, packed i8
17+;; truncation, memmove-style array.copy) the reference reproduces them.
18+;;
19+;; Representation under native lg: struct and array instances are Go-backed
20+;; object-arrays whose slot 0 is the type's declaration map; an i31 is a
21+;; two-slot array tagged i31-tag; a funcref is [sig f]; null is nil.
22+(ns wasm.intrinsics
23+ (:refer-clojure :exclude [get set! aget new]))
24+
25+(def ^:private array-type (type (object-array 0)))
26+(def ^:private i31-tag {::kind :i31 :name 'i31})
27+
28+(defn- trap!
29+ "Raise the reference impl's stand-in for a wasm trap. Runtime code must
30+ never catch these: in wasm a trap is not an exception."
31+ [msg data]
32+ (throw (ex-info (str "wasm trap: " msg) (assoc data :wasm/trap true))))
33+
34+(defn- tagged? [x]
35+ (and (= (type x) array-type)
36+ (pos? (alength x))
37+ (map? (core/aget x 0))
38+ (some? (::kind (core/aget x 0)))))
39+
40+(defn- kind-name [x]
41+ (cond (nil? x) "null"
42+ (tagged? x) (str (name (::kind (core/aget x 0))) " " (:name (core/aget x 0)))
43+ :else (str "non-wasm value " (pr-str x) " (" (type x) ")")))
44+
45+(defn- eqref? [x]
46+ ;; A native exception is the reference's stand-in for the payload a wasm
47+ ;; `catch $lgex` binds, which is always a (ref null eq): runtime code may
48+ ;; keep what it caught (a LazySeq caches its thunk's error, D74).
49+ (or (nil? x) (and (tagged? x) (not= :func (::kind (core/aget x 0)))) (instance? Throwable x)))
50+
51+(defn- funcref? [x]
52+ (or (nil? x) (and (tagged? x) (= :func (::kind (core/aget x 0))))))
53+
54+(defn- check-ref! [who x]
55+ (when-not (eqref? x)
56+ (throw (ex-info (str who ": expected a wasm ref, got " (kind-name x)) {:who who}))))
57+
58+(defn- check-int! [who x]
59+ (when-not (int? x)
60+ (throw (ex-info (str who ": expected i64 (lg int), got " (pr-str x)) {:who who})))
61+ x)
62+
63+(def ^:private i32-min -2147483648)
64+(def ^:private i32-max 2147483647)
65+
66+(defn- check-val!
67+ "A value stored into a field/element of wasm type t must already be that
68+ type; the backend inserts no conversions at a store."
69+ [who t v]
70+ (case t
71+ :i64 (check-int! who v)
72+ :i32 (when-not (and (int? v) (<= i32-min v i32-max))
73+ (throw (ex-info (str who ": i32 slot needs an int in [-2^31, 2^31), got " (pr-str v)
74+ " (use i32-wrap first)") {:who who})))
75+ :f64 (when-not (float? v)
76+ (throw (ex-info (str who ": f64 slot needs a float, got " (pr-str v)) {:who who})))
77+ :i8 (when-not (and (int? v) (<= 0 v 255))
78+ (throw (ex-info (str who ": i8 slot needs an int in [0, 256), got " (pr-str v)) {:who who})))
79+ :ref (check-ref! who v)
80+ :funcref (when-not (funcref? v)
81+ (throw (ex-info (str who ": funcref slot got " (kind-name v)) {:who who})))
82+ (throw (ex-info (str who ": unknown slot type " t) {:who who})))
83+ v)
84+
85+(defn- check-index! [who i n]
86+ (check-int! who i)
87+ (when-not (and (<= 0 i) (< i n))
88+ (trap! (str who ": index " i " out of bounds for length " n) {:who who :index i :length n})))
89+
90+;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
91+;; Declarations. Field types are :i64 :f64 :i32 :ref :funcref; a mutable
92+;; field is written [:mut <type>]. The backend reads these defs as a data table
93+;; and emits one (rec ...) group, so types are nominal by position even when
94+;; two declarations have the same field list (wasm canonicalises structurally
95+;; identical types across rec groups; inside one group they stay distinct).
96+
97+(def ^:private slot-types #{:i64 :f64 :i32 :ref :funcref})
98+
99+(defn struct-decl [nm fields]
100+ (let [norm (mapv (fn [f]
101+ (let [[mut? t] (if (vector? f)
102+ (if (and (= 2 (count f)) (= :mut (first f)))
103+ [true (second f)]
104+ (throw (ex-info (str "defstruct " nm ": bad field " (pr-str f)) {})))
105+ [false f])]
106+ (when-not (slot-types t)
107+ (throw (ex-info (str "defstruct " nm ": bad field type " (pr-str t)) {})))
108+ {:type t :mut mut?}))
109+ fields)]
110+ {::kind :struct :name nm :fields norm}))
111+
112+(defn array-decl [nm elem]
113+ (when-not (slot-types elem)
114+ (throw (ex-info (str "defarray " nm ": bad element type " (pr-str elem)) {})))
115+ {::kind :array :name nm :elem elem})
116+
117+(defn func-decl [nm params result]
118+ (doseq [t (conj (vec params) result)]
119+ (when-not (slot-types t)
120+ (throw (ex-info (str "deffunc " nm ": bad type " (pr-str t)) {}))))
121+ {::kind :func :name nm :params (vec params) :result result})
122+
123+(defmacro defstruct
124+ "(defstruct Name [field-type ...]) => (type $Name (struct (field ...) ...))."
125+ [nm fields]
126+ `(def ~nm (struct-decl '~nm ~fields)))
127+
128+(defmacro defarray
129+ "(defarray Name elem-type) => (type $Name (array (mut elem-type)))."
130+ [nm elem]
131+ `(def ~nm (array-decl '~nm ~elem)))
132+
133+(defmacro deffunc
134+ "(deffunc Name [param-type ...] result-type) => (type $Name (func ...))."
135+ [nm params result]
136+ `(def ~nm (func-decl '~nm ~params ~result)))
137+
138+;; The built-in byte array: strings are (array (mut i8)) per D5.
139+(def Bytes {::kind :array :name 'Bytes :elem :i8})
140+
141+(defn- check-decl! [who decl k]
142+ (when-not (and (map? decl) (= k (::kind decl)))
143+ (throw (ex-info (str who ": expected a " (name k) " declaration, got " (pr-str decl)) {:who who}))))
144+
145+(defn- instance-of? [decl x]
146+ (and (tagged? x) (identical? decl (core/aget x 0))))
147+
148+(defn- cast! [who decl x]
149+ (when-not (instance-of? decl x)
150+ (trap! (str who ": cast failure, expected " (name (::kind decl)) " " (:name decl)
151+ ", got " (kind-name x))
152+ {:who who :expected (:name decl)}))
153+ x)
154+
155+;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
156+;; Structs
157+
158+(defn- new* [decl vals]
159+ (check-decl! "wasm/new" decl :struct)
160+ (let [fs (:fields decl)]
161+ (when-not (= (count fs) (count vals))
162+ (throw (ex-info (str "wasm/new " (:name decl) ": " (count fs) " fields, got " (count vals)) {})))
163+ (let [a (object-array (inc (count fs)))]
164+ (core/aset a 0 decl)
165+ (dotimes [i (count fs)]
166+ (core/aset a (inc i) (check-val! (str "wasm/new " (:name decl) " field " i)
167+ (:type (nth fs i)) (nth vals i))))
168+ a)))
169+
170+(defn ^{:intrinsic true :wasm "struct.new $Name" :type "[decl fields...] -> :any"} new
171+ "(new Name f1 ... fn) => struct.new $Name. Arity is the field count; the
172+ backend sees it statically. Multi-arity only because a struct's operand
173+ count is its declaration's."
174+ ([decl] (new* decl []))
175+ ([decl a] (new* decl [a]))
176+ ([decl a b] (new* decl [a b]))
177+ ([decl a b c] (new* decl [a b c]))
178+ ([decl a b c d] (new* decl [a b c d]))
179+ ([decl a b c d e] (new* decl [a b c d e]))
180+ ([decl a b c d e f] (new* decl [a b c d e f]))
181+ ([decl a b c d e f g] (new* decl [a b c d e f g])))
182+
183+(defn- check-field! [who decl idx]
184+ (when-not (and (int? idx) (<= 0 idx) (< idx (count (:fields decl))))
185+ (throw (ex-info (str who " " (:name decl) ": field index " (pr-str idx) " out of range 0.."
186+ (dec (count (:fields decl)))) {:who who}))))
187+
188+(defn ^{:intrinsic true :wasm "ref.cast (ref $Name); struct.get $Name idx (i32 field: i64.extend_i32_s)"
189+ :type "[decl const-int :any] -> field type"} get
190+ "(get Name idx x): idx is a literal. Traps on null or a non-Name x."
191+ [decl idx x]
192+ (check-decl! "wasm/get" decl :struct)
193+ (check-field! "wasm/get" decl idx)
194+ (cast! "wasm/get" decl x)
195+ (core/aget x (inc idx)))
196+
197+(defn ^{:intrinsic true :wasm "ref.cast (ref $Name); struct.set $Name idx"
198+ :type "[decl const-int :any T] -> :nil"} set!
199+ "(set! Name idx x v): only for fields declared [:mut t]."
200+ [decl idx x v]
201+ (check-decl! "wasm/set!" decl :struct)
202+ (check-field! "wasm/set!" decl idx)
203+ (when-not (:mut (nth (:fields decl) idx))
204+ (throw (ex-info (str "wasm/set! " (:name decl) ": field " idx " is immutable") {})))
205+ (cast! "wasm/set!" decl x)
206+ (core/aset x (inc idx) (check-val! "wasm/set!" (:type (nth (:fields decl) idx)) v))
207+ nil)
208+
209+(defn ^{:intrinsic true :wasm "ref.test (ref $Name)" :type "[decl :any] -> :bool"} is?
210+ [decl x]
211+ (when-not (#{:struct :array} (::kind decl))
212+ (throw (ex-info (str "wasm/is?: not a type declaration " (pr-str decl)) {})))
213+ (check-ref! "wasm/is?" x)
214+ (instance-of? decl x))
215+
216+(defn ^{:intrinsic true :wasm "ref.cast (ref $Name)" :type "[decl :any] -> :any"} as
217+ "Traps on null and on any other type, naming both."
218+ [decl x]
219+ (when-not (#{:struct :array} (::kind decl))
220+ (throw (ex-info (str "wasm/as: not a type declaration " (pr-str decl)) {})))
221+ (check-ref! "wasm/as" x)
222+ (cast! "wasm/as" decl x))
223+
224+;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
225+;; Arrays
226+
227+(def ^:private max-array-len 2147483647)
228+
229+(defn ^{:intrinsic true :wasm "array.new $Name (len: i32.wrap_i64)" :type "[decl :int T] -> :any"} array-new
230+ [decl len init]
231+ (check-decl! "wasm/array-new" decl :array)
232+ (check-int! "wasm/array-new" len)

429+(defn- utf8-decode [b]
430+ (let [n (dec (alength b))
431+ at (fn [i] (if (< i n) (core/aget b (inc i)) (trap! "string-of-bytes: truncated UTF-8" {})))
432+ cont (fn [i] (let [c (at i)]
433+ (when-not (= 0x80 (bit-and c 0xC0)) (trap! "string-of-bytes: bad continuation byte" {:at i}))
434+ (bit-and c 0x3F)))]
435+ (loop [i 0 out []]
436+ (if (>= i n)
437+ (apply str out)
438+ (let [c (at i)
439+ [cp len] (cond (< c 0x80) [c 1]
440+ (= 0xC0 (bit-and c 0xE0)) [(+ (* (bit-and c 0x1F) 64) (cont (inc i))) 2]
441+ ;; lg's bit-or is binary; the bit groups are disjoint, so + composes them.
442+ (= 0xE0 (bit-and c 0xF0)) [(+ (* (bit-and c 0x0F) 4096) (* (cont (inc i)) 64) (cont (+ i 2))) 3]
443+ (= 0xF0 (bit-and c 0xF8)) [(+ (* (bit-and c 0x07) 262144) (* (cont (inc i)) 4096)
444+ (* (cont (+ i 2)) 64) (cont (+ i 3))) 4]
445+ :else (trap! "string-of-bytes: bad lead byte" {:at i}))]
446+ (when (or (and (= len 2) (< cp 0x80)) (and (= len 3) (< cp 0x800)) (and (= len 4) (< cp 0x10000))
447+ (<= 0xD800 cp 0xDFFF) (> cp 0x10FFFF))
448+ (trap! "string-of-bytes: overlong, surrogate or out-of-range code point" {:at i :cp cp}))
449+ (recur (+ i len) (conj out (char cp))))))))

504+(defn- call-ref* [sig fr args]

506+ (when (nil? fr) (trap! "wasm/call-ref: null funcref" {}))

509+ (when-not (= (count args) (count (:params sig)))

516+ count is its signature's; each call site's count is static."

518+ ([sig fr a] (call-ref* sig fr [a]))
519+ ([sig fr a b] (call-ref* sig fr [a b]))
520+ ([sig fr a b c] (call-ref* sig fr [a b c]))
521+ ([sig fr a b c d] (call-ref* sig fr [a b c d]))

116+;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
117+;; ->AssertionError: an exception carrying the message (0 to 2 args; a
118+;; cause is kept only if it is an exception). Raised as wasm.core's raw
119+;; error (kind 1), so the uncaught text and ex-message match native; its
120+;; class is not modelled: native prints it as #error {:type
121+;; java.lang.AssertionError ...}, reports that type, and is not caught by
122+;; (catch Exception ...), which here it is.

126+ (= 17 (sq/kind msg))
127+ (wasm/new sq/Err 1 (s/str-bytes msg) (s/str-bytes msg) (wasm/null)
128+ (if (wasm/null? cause) (wasm/null) (if (= 26 (sq/kind cause)) cause (wasm/null))))
129+ :else (raise-str (s/str (lit (wasm/bytes-of-string "java.lang.AssertionError. expected a String message, got "))

132+(defn ^{:twin "core/->AssertionError"} assertion-error
133+ ([] (assertion false (wasm/null) (wasm/null)))
134+ ([msg] (assertion true msg (wasm/null)))
135+ ([msg cause] (assertion true msg cause))
136+ ([a b x] (c/raise (wasm/bytes-of-string "java.lang.AssertionError. expects 0 to 2 args, got 3"))))

10+;; Go's PORTABLE algorithms (math/exp.go, log.go, pow.go, sqrt.go, mod.go,
11+;; frexp.go, ldexp.go, floor.go), each operation rounded separately: that

1+;; wasm.phm — let-go's PersistentMap (pkg/vm/persistent_map.go at 4e769212)
2+;; and its TransientMap (pkg/vm/transient.go), written in the runtime dialect
3+;; (see wasm.pvec's header): IR special forms, IR-op core fns on :int, this
4+;; file's own fns, wasm.intrinsics, and the runtime it shares a value model
5+;; with: wasm.seq (D38: Int/Bool boxes, `kind`, `equiv?`, `hash`) and
6+;; wasm.pvec (a map entry is a 2-element vector, as MapEntry is an
7+;; ArrayVector, persistent_map.go:61).
8+;;
9+;; Structure is mirrored, not reinvented, because structure IS the iteration
10+;; order: an ordered array-map mode up to 8 entries, then a HAMT of bitmap
11+;; nodes and collision nodes only (let-go has no ArrayNode), walked slot by
12+;; slot. Go line numbers are cited at each function; corpus/maporder/SPEC.md
13+;; has the order rules they produce.
14+;;
15+;; Representation differences that do not change behaviour:
16+;; - Go marks a child slot with a Go-nil key. Here lg nil IS wasm null (D2),
17+;; so a nil key could not be told apart; a slot is a child when its value
18+;; slot holds a node struct (`node?`), which no map value can be.
19+;; - Go's transient nodes keep slack capacity (persistent_map.go:354-364,
20+;; :410-436); here arrays are exact-length and an insert reallocates. The
21+;; contents, and so the order, are the same.
22+;; - Lookup returns a caller-chosen not-found sentinel instead of (v, ok).
23+;; - Errors Go returns (transient used after persistent!) are raised as D68
24+;; Errs (P2.13).
25+;;
26+;; Natives here take and return refs per D37 only at the seq.lg hook boundary
27+;; (install-hooks! below, slot 0); the map API itself takes :int/:bool where Go's
28+;; does (mcount, mcontains?), which the backend boxes at a call site.
29+;;
30+;; seq: `entries` returns a fresh HSlots array [k0 v0 k1 v1 ...] in seq order,
31+;; which is what Go's Seq materialises (persistent_map.go:1002-1023) before
32+;; wrapping it in a MapSeq; `entry-seq` turns that into seq.lg's MapSeq
33+;; (kind 27) over MapEntry values for the `seq` hook (R5, P2.13).
34+(ns wasm.phm
35+ (:require [wasm.intrinsics :as wasm]
36+ [wasm.pvec :as pv]
37+ [wasm.seq :as sq]))

39+(wasm/defarray HSlots :ref)
40+;; count, root (null = ordered array-map mode, persistent_map.go:629),
41+;; okvs (ordered mode: exactly 2*count slots; HAMT mode: null), hash cache (-1 = none),
42+;; meta (null = none; assoc/dissoc keep it, persistent! of a transient drops it).
43+(wasm/defstruct HMap [:i64 :ref :ref [:mut :i64] :ref])
44+;; bitmap, edit token (null = persistent), pairs [key val] or [null child].
45+(wasm/defstruct HBitmapNode [[:mut :i64] :ref [:mut :ref]])
46+;; hash, count, pairs in insertion order (persistent_map.go:489-493).
47+(wasm/defstruct HCollisionNode [:i64 :i64 :ref])

49+;; (1 while editable, 0 after persistent!; transient.go:23).

51+;; edit (HFlag), root, okvs (ordered mode, capacity 2*(max+1)), hamt (0/1), count.
52+(wasm/defstruct HTransient [:ref [:mut :ref] [:mut :ref] [:mut :i32] [:mut :i64]])

72+;; Key hash and equality: hashValue and valueEquiv (hash.go:23, :143-210).

74+;; Go Equals method (ArrayVector/PersistentVector/MapEntry, PersistentMap),
75+;; that decides, and Equals takes only its own kind: a vector equals only a
76+;; vector (elements by `=`), a map only a map (values by valueEquiv). Any
77+;; other first operand falls back to `=`. So {:a [1]} != {:a '(1)} but

1+;; wasm.pvec — P2.1's sufficiency proof: a persistent vector (32-way trie
2+;; plus tail, the PersistentVector shape of pkg/vm/vector.go and CLJS) written
3+;; in the runtime dialect: only IR special forms, IR-op core fns on :int
4+;; (+ - inc dec < <= > >= = bit-and unsigned-bit-shift-right
5+;; bit-shift-left), macros that expand to those, calls to this file's own
6+;; fns, and wasm.intrinsics. No nil?, not, core collections or interop.
7+;; Elements are refs (box ints with wasm/i31). Out-of-range access traps;
8+;; the catchable lg exception arrives with ex-info in P2.7.
9+(ns wasm.pvec
10+ (:require [wasm.intrinsics :as wasm]))
11+
12+;; pkind (D73) records which Go type native would hold: 0 ArrayVector
13+;; (literals, vec, subvec, persistent! up to 32, conj up to 32), 1
14+;; PersistentVector (conj past 32, with-meta, persistent! past 32). Native
15+;; never demotes a PersistentVector, so conj/assoc/pop keep it; hash, print,
16+;; type and the seq view all depend on it (rt/wasm/README.md).
17+(wasm/defstruct PVec [:i64 :i64 :ref :ref :ref :i64]) ; cnt, shift, root, tail, meta (null = none), pkind
18+(wasm/defarray Node :ref) ; trie node (32 slots) or tail (1..32)
19+
20+(defn- node-clone [src n]
21+ (let [dst (wasm/array-new Node n (wasm/null))]
22+ (wasm/array-copy Node dst 0 src 0 (if (< (wasm/alen src) n) (wasm/alen src) n))
23+ dst))
24+
25+(defn empty-vec []
26+ (wasm/new PVec 0 5 (wasm/array-new Node 32 (wasm/null)) (wasm/array-new Node 0 (wasm/null)) (wasm/null) 0))
27+
28+(defn vmeta [v] (wasm/get PVec 4 v))
29+(defn vpkind [v] ; 0 ArrayVector, 1 PersistentVector (D73)
30+ (wasm/get PVec 5 v))
31+(defn vretag [v pk m] ; v's trie as kind pk with meta m (shared)
32+ (wasm/new PVec (wasm/get PVec 0 v) (wasm/get PVec 1 v) (wasm/get PVec 2 v) (wasm/get PVec 3 v) m pk))
33+(defn varray [v] ; an ArrayVector without meta: what vec, subvec and a literal build at any size
34+ (vretag v 0 (wasm/null)))
35+(defn vwith-meta [v m] ; with-meta: the trie is shared; ArrayVector.WithMeta promotes
36+ (vretag v 1 m))
37+
38+(defn- mk [v cnt shift root tail] ; a successor of v: same meta and kind
39+ (wasm/new PVec cnt shift root tail (wasm/get PVec 4 v) (wasm/get PVec 5 v)))
40+
41+(defn vcount [v] (wasm/get PVec 0 v))
42+
43+(defn- tailoff [cnt]
44+ (if (< cnt 32) 0 (bit-shift-left (unsigned-bit-shift-right (dec cnt) 5) 5)))
45+
46+(defn- array-for [v i]
47+ (if (>= i (tailoff (wasm/get PVec 0 v)))
48+ (wasm/get PVec 3 v)
49+ (loop [node (wasm/get PVec 2 v) level (wasm/get PVec 1 v)]
50+ (if (> level 0)
51+ (recur (wasm/aget Node node (bit-and (unsigned-bit-shift-right i level) 31)) (- level 5))
52+ node))))
53+
54+(defn- check-index [v i]
55+ (if (if (< i 0) true (>= i (wasm/get PVec 0 v)))
56+ (wasm/trap "pvec: index out of bounds")
57+ nil))
58+
59+(defn vnth [v i]
60+ (check-index v i)
61+ (wasm/aget Node (array-for v i) (bit-and i 31)))
62+
63+(defn- new-path [level node]
64+ (if (= level 0)
65+ node
66+ (let [r (wasm/array-new Node 32 (wasm/null))]
67+ (wasm/aset! Node r 0 (new-path (- level 5) node))
68+ r)))
69+
70+(defn- push-tail [cnt level parent tail-node]
71+ (let [subidx (bit-and (unsigned-bit-shift-right (dec cnt) level) 31)
72+ ret (node-clone parent 32)]
73+ (if (= level 5)
74+ (wasm/aset! Node ret subidx tail-node)
75+ (let [child (wasm/aget Node parent subidx)]
76+ (wasm/aset! Node ret subidx
77+ (if (wasm/null? child)
78+ (new-path (- level 5) tail-node)
79+ (push-tail cnt (- level 5) child tail-node)))))
80+ ret))
81+
82+(defn vconj [v x]
83+ (let [cnt (wasm/get PVec 0 v) shift (wasm/get PVec 1 v)
84+ root (wasm/get PVec 2 v) tail (wasm/get PVec 3 v)
85+ ;; ArrayVector.Conj promotes once the result passes 32 (vector.go:39)
86+ pk (if (= 1 (wasm/get PVec 5 v)) 1 (if (> (inc cnt) 32) 1 0))]
87+ (if (< (- cnt (tailoff cnt)) 32)
88+ (let [nt (node-clone tail (inc (wasm/alen tail)))]
89+ (wasm/aset! Node nt (wasm/alen tail) x)
90+ (wasm/new PVec (inc cnt) shift root nt (vmeta v) pk))
91+ (let [nt (wasm/array-new Node 1 x)]
92+ (if (> (unsigned-bit-shift-right cnt 5) (bit-shift-left 1 shift))
93+ (let [nr (wasm/array-new Node 32 (wasm/null))]
94+ (wasm/aset! Node nr 0 root)
95+ (wasm/aset! Node nr 1 (new-path shift tail))
96+ (wasm/new PVec (inc cnt) (+ shift 5) nr nt (vmeta v) pk))
97+ (wasm/new PVec (inc cnt) shift (push-tail cnt shift root tail) nt (vmeta v) pk))))))
98+
99+(defn- do-assoc [level node i x]
100+ (let [ret (node-clone node 32)]
101+ (if (= level 0)
102+ (wasm/aset! Node ret (bit-and i 31) x)
103+ (let [subidx (bit-and (unsigned-bit-shift-right i level) 31)]
104+ (wasm/aset! Node ret subidx (do-assoc (- level 5) (wasm/aget Node node subidx) i x))))
105+ ret))
106+
107+(defn vassoc [v i x]
108+ (let [cnt (wasm/get PVec 0 v)]
109+ (if (= i cnt)
110+ (vconj v x)
111+ (do (check-index v i)
112+ (if (>= i (tailoff cnt))
113+ (let [tail (wasm/get PVec 3 v) nt (node-clone tail (wasm/alen tail))]
114+ (wasm/aset! Node nt (bit-and i 31) x)
115+ (mk v cnt (wasm/get PVec 1 v) (wasm/get PVec 2 v) nt))
116+ (mk v cnt (wasm/get PVec 1 v)
117+ (do-assoc (wasm/get PVec 1 v) (wasm/get PVec 2 v) i x)
118+ (wasm/get PVec 3 v)))))))
119+
120+(defn- pop-tail [cnt level node]
121+ (let [subidx (bit-and (unsigned-bit-shift-right (- cnt 2) level) 31)]
122+ (if (> level 5)
123+ (let [nc (pop-tail cnt (- level 5) (wasm/aget Node node subidx))]
124+ (if (if (wasm/null? nc) (= subidx 0) false)
125+ (wasm/null)
126+ (let [ret (node-clone node 32)]
127+ (wasm/aset! Node ret subidx nc)
128+ ret)))
129+ (if (= subidx 0)
130+ (wasm/null)
131+ (let [ret (node-clone node 32)]
132+ (wasm/aset! Node ret subidx (wasm/null))
133+ ret)))))
134+
135+(defn vpop [v]
136+ (let [cnt (wasm/get PVec 0 v) shift (wasm/get PVec 1 v)
137+ root (wasm/get PVec 2 v) tail (wasm/get PVec 3 v)]
138+ (cond
139+ (= cnt 0) (wasm/trap "pvec: can't pop empty vector")
140+ (= cnt 1) (vretag (empty-vec) (wasm/get PVec 5 v) (vmeta v)) ; PersistentVector.Pop keeps kind and meta
141+ (> (- cnt (tailoff cnt)) 1)
142+ (mk v (dec cnt) shift root (node-clone tail (dec (wasm/alen tail))))
143+ :else
144+ (let [nt (array-for v (- cnt 2))
145+ nr0 (pop-tail cnt shift root)
146+ nr (if (wasm/null? nr0) (wasm/array-new Node 32 (wasm/null)) nr0)]
147+ (if (if (> shift 5) (wasm/null? (wasm/aget Node nr 1)) false)
148+ (mk v (dec cnt) (- shift 5) (wasm/aget Node nr 0) nt)
149+ (mk v (dec cnt) shift nr nt))))))

@@ -0,0 +1,991 @@
1+;; wasm.reader — P3.0: `read-string` for data, in the runtime dialect of
2+;; seq.lg (IR special forms, IR-op core fns on :int and :float, macros
3+;; expanding to those, wasm.intrinsics, and the other runtime namespaces).
4+;; A near-literal port of let-go's data reader (core/read-string =
5+;; newDataReaderWithResolvers + ReadSkipNoValue, pkg/compiler/eval.go:241)
6+;; at 4e769212: pkg/compiler/reader.go and errors.go, plus Go's strconv
7+;; (ParseInt, ParseFloat via its exact `decimal` path) and fmt's %x/%o scan
8+;; for the cases the reader hands to them. READER.md has the grammar, the
9+;; token table, every error message with its citation, and the named limits.
10+;;
11+;; Shape: one reader state per call (RS + Aux; `new` takes at most 8
12+;; fields). Read functions return a value, the state's Void marker (a form
13+;; that reads as nothing: comment, discard), or the state itself on failure,
14+;; with the message chain in Aux. That mirrors Go's (Value, error) returns
15+;; without try/catch, and it is what lets `#_` swallow a non-EOF error the
16+;; way readFormComment does. The chain is built exactly as ReaderError.Error
17+;; + errors.AddCause print it: "Syntax error reading source at
18+;; (<read-string>:L:C).\n<msg>" then "\n\tcaused by <inner>" per Wrap.
19+;; Line and column are tracked as LispReader.next/unread do (runes, not
20+;; bytes; unread of a newline restores the previous column).
21+;;
22+;; Errors: the final chain is raised as the backend's exception value via
23+;; wasm.core/raise (D68), msg = cmsg as for any native called as a value.
24+;; Named limits (values the runtime has no box for, reader features that
25+;; need *ns* or *data-readers*) are raised the same way, catchable, with a
26+;; "lower-wasm: " message, because read-string's input is user data (xsofy's
27+;; console wraps it in try).
28+(ns wasm.reader
29+ (:refer-clojure :exclude [read-string])
30+ (:require [wasm.intrinsics :as wasm]
31+ [wasm.pvec :as pv]
32+ [wasm.seq :as sq]
33+ [wasm.str :as s]
34+ [wasm.phm :as m]
35+ [wasm.phs :as hs]
36+ [wasm.core :as c]))
37+
38+;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
39+;; State (`new` takes at most 7 fields). RS: input bytes, length, byte
40+;; position, rune position (Go's r.pos), line, column, Aux. Aux: lastCol,
41+;; lastRune, lastSize, error chain (Str), caused-by-EOF flag, the Void
42+;; marker, and the :line/:column keywords (Kws).
43+(wasm/defstruct RS [:ref :i64 [:mut :i64] [:mut :i64] [:mut :i64] [:mut :i64] :ref])
44+(wasm/defstruct Aux [[:mut :i64] [:mut :i64] [:mut :i64] [:mut :ref] [:mut :i64] :ref :ref])
45+(wasm/defstruct Kws [:ref :ref])
46+(wasm/defstruct Void [:i64])
47+(wasm/defstruct RBuf [[:mut :ref] [:mut :i64]]) ; bytes, length
48+(wasm/defstruct RDec [:ref [:mut :i64] [:mut :i64] [:mut :i64]]) ; strconv decimal: digits 0..9, nd, dp, trunc
49+
50+(defn- st-new [bs from]
51+ (wasm/new RS bs (wasm/alen bs) from 0 0 0
52+ (wasm/new Aux 0 -1 0 (wasm/null) 0 (wasm/new Void 0)
53+ (wasm/new Kws (s/kw-of-bytes (wasm/bytes-of-string "line"))
54+ (s/kw-of-bytes (wasm/bytes-of-string "column"))))))
55+(defn- aux [st] (wasm/get RS 6 st))
56+(defn- void [st] (wasm/get Aux 5 (aux st)))
57+(defn- failed? [st v] (wasm/ref-eq v st))
58+(defn- void? [st v] (wasm/ref-eq v (void st)))
59+
60+;; LispReader.next (reader.go:151): -1 at EOF, nothing consumed.
61+(defn- next! [st]
62+ (let [pos (wasm/get RS 2 st) n (wasm/get RS 1 st)]
63+ (if (>= pos n)
64+ -1
65+ (let [d (sq/decode-at (wasm/get RS 0 st) pos n)
66+ r (unsigned-bit-shift-right d 3)
67+ ax (aux st)]
68+ (wasm/set! RS 2 st (+ pos (bit-and d 7)))
69+ (wasm/set! RS 3 st (inc (wasm/get RS 3 st)))
70+ (if (= r 10)
71+ (do (wasm/set! RS 4 st (inc (wasm/get RS 4 st)))
72+ (wasm/set! Aux 0 ax (wasm/get RS 5 st))
73+ (wasm/set! RS 5 st 0))
74+ (wasm/set! RS 5 st (inc (wasm/get RS 5 st))))
75+ (wasm/set! Aux 1 ax r)
76+ (wasm/set! Aux 2 ax (bit-and d 7))
77+ r))))
78+
79+;; LispReader.unread (reader.go:167): one rune back.
80+(defn- unread! [st]
81+ (let [ax (aux st)]
82+ (wasm/set! RS 2 st (- (wasm/get RS 2 st) (wasm/get Aux 2 ax)))
83+ (wasm/set! RS 3 st (dec (wasm/get RS 3 st)))
84+ (if (= 10 (wasm/get Aux 1 ax))
85+ (do (wasm/set! RS 4 st (dec (wasm/get RS 4 st))) (wasm/set! RS 5 st (wasm/get Aux 0 ax)))
86+ (wasm/set! RS 5 st (dec (wasm/get RS 5 st))))))
87+
88+;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
89+;; Errors. Each returns st, the failure marker.
90+
91+(defn- header [st] ; ReaderError.Error (errors.go:37)
92+ (s/str (s/str (s/lit "Syntax error reading source at (<read-string>:")
93+ (sq/box-int (inc (wasm/get RS 4 st))) (s/lit ":"))
94+ (sq/box-int (inc (wasm/get RS 5 st)))
95+ (s/lit ").\n")))
96+
97+;; The chain is kept as a pvec of layers, innermost first, and joined once
98+;; when raised: a 200-deep EOF wraps 200 times, and joining at every wrap
99+;; would copy the growing chain each time.
100+(defn- layer [st msg] (s/str (header st) msg))
101+
102+(defn- fail! [st msg] ; NewReaderError(r, msg), no cause
103+ (wasm/set! Aux 3 (aux st) (pv/vconj (pv/empty-vec) (layer st msg)))
104+ (wasm/set! Aux 4 (aux st) 0)
105+ st)
106+
107+(defn- fail-eof! [st msg] ; NewReaderError(r, msg).Wrap(io.EOF)
108+ (wasm/set! Aux 3 (aux st) (pv/vconj (pv/vconj (pv/empty-vec) (s/lit "EOF")) (layer st msg)))
109+ (wasm/set! Aux 4 (aux st) 1)
110+ st)
111+
112+(defn- wrap! [st msg] ; NewReaderError(r, msg).Wrap(err)
113+ (wasm/set! Aux 3 (aux st) (pv/vconj (wasm/get Aux 3 (aux st)) (layer st msg)))
114+ st)
115+
116+(defn- limit [what] ; a named limit, catchable (see the header)
117+ (c/raise (s/str-bytes (s/str (s/lit "lower-wasm: read-string: ") what))))
118+
119+;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
120+;; Bytes and a growable byte buffer (str.lg's are private; READER.md, Dedupe).
121+
122+(defn- slice [bs from to]
123+ (let [out (wasm/bytes-new (- to from))]
124+ (wasm/array-copy wasm/Bytes out 0 bs from (- to from))
125+ out))
126+
127+(defn- buf-new [] (wasm/new RBuf (wasm/bytes-new 16) 0))
128+
129+(defn- buf-byte! [b v]
130+ (let [bs (wasm/get RBuf 0 b) len (wasm/get RBuf 1 b)]
131+ (when (>= len (wasm/alen bs))
132+ (let [nb (wasm/bytes-new (* 2 (wasm/alen bs)))]
133+ (wasm/array-copy wasm/Bytes nb 0 bs 0 len)
134+ (wasm/set! RBuf 0 b nb)))
135+ (wasm/bset! (wasm/get RBuf 0 b) len v)
136+ (wasm/set! RBuf 1 b (inc len))))
137+
138+(defn- buf-rune! [b r] ; strings.Builder.WriteRune: invalid -> U+FFFD
139+ (let [r (if (if (< r 0) true (if (> r 0x10FFFF) true (if (>= r 0xD800) (<= r 0xDFFF) false))) 0xFFFD r)]
140+ (cond (< r 0x80) (buf-byte! b r)
141+ (< r 0x800) (do (buf-byte! b (+ 0xC0 (unsigned-bit-shift-right r 6)))
142+ (buf-byte! b (+ 0x80 (bit-and r 0x3F))))
143+ (< r 0x10000) (do (buf-byte! b (+ 0xE0 (unsigned-bit-shift-right r 12)))
144+ (buf-byte! b (+ 0x80 (bit-and (unsigned-bit-shift-right r 6) 0x3F)))
145+ (buf-byte! b (+ 0x80 (bit-and r 0x3F))))
146+ :else (do (buf-byte! b (+ 0xF0 (unsigned-bit-shift-right r 18)))
147+ (buf-byte! b (+ 0x80 (bit-and (unsigned-bit-shift-right r 12) 0x3F)))
148+ (buf-byte! b (+ 0x80 (bit-and (unsigned-bit-shift-right r 6) 0x3F)))
149+ (buf-byte! b (+ 0x80 (bit-and r 0x3F)))))))
150+
151+(defn- buf-bytes [b] (slice (wasm/get RBuf 0 b) 0 (wasm/get RBuf 1 b)))
152+
153+(defn- bytes-is? [bs lit] ; bs equals a literal's bytes
154+ (sq/bytes-eq? bs lit))
155+
156+(defn- hex-digit [d] (if (< d 10) (+ 48 d) (+ 55 d)))
157+
158+(defn- hex4 [v] ; fmt %04X of a non-negative int

160+ nd (loop [k 4 x (unsigned-bit-shift-right v 16)] (if (> x 0) (recur (inc k) (unsigned-bit-shift-right x 4)) k))]

162+ (when (>= i 0)
163+ (buf-byte! b (hex-digit (bit-and (unsigned-bit-shift-right v (* 4 i)) 15)))
164+ (recur (dec i))))
165+ (s/mk-str (buf-bytes b))))

167+;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
168+;; Character classes (reader.go:1887-1901). unicode.IsSpace and
169+;; unicode.IsDigit beyond ASCII come from Go 1.27's tables: White_Space

171+;; U+3000) and category Nd, encoded below as 6 hex digits of the first code
172+;; point and 2 of (run length - 1); every run is 10 long except U+116D0 (20)
173+;; and U+1D7CE (50).

175+(defn- whitespace? [r] ; isWhitespace: unicode.IsSpace or ','

177+ (= r 0x85) true
178+ (= r 0xA0) true
179+ (= r 0x1680) true
180+ (if (>= r 0x2000) (<= r 0x200A) false) true
181+ (if (= r 0x2028) true (if (= r 0x2029) true (if (= r 0x202F) true (if (= r 0x205F) true (= r 0x3000))))) true
182+ :else false))
183+
184+(defn- hexval [c] ; ASCII hex digit value, -1 otherwise
185+ (cond (if (>= c 48) (<= c 57) false) (- c 48)
186+ (if (>= c 97) (<= c 102) false) (- c 87)
187+ (if (>= c 65) (<= c 70) false) (- c 55)
188+ :else -1))
189+
190+(defn- nd-digit? [r] ; unicode.IsDigit

192+ (if (>= r 48) (<= r 57) false)

194+ n (wasm/alen t)]
195+ (loop [i 0]
196+ (if (< i n)
197+ (let [lo (loop [j 0 v 0] (if (< j 6) (recur (inc j) (+ (* v 16) (hexval (wasm/bget t (+ i j))))) v))
198+ len (+ (* 16 (hexval (wasm/bget t (+ i 6)))) (hexval (wasm/bget t (+ i 7))))]

201+
202+(defn- hex-rune? [r] ; isHexDigit: unicode.IsDigit or a-f A-F
203+ (if (nd-digit? r) true (if (if (>= r 97) (<= r 102) false) true (if (>= r 65) (<= r 70) false))))
204+
205+(defn- macro? [r] ; the macros table (reader.go:1921)

207+ (= r 34) true (= r 92) true (= r 39) true (= r 64) true (= r 96) true (= r 126) true

209+ :else false))
210+
211+(defn- terminating? [r] ; isTerminatingMacro: a macro other than # ' %
212+ (if (= r 35) false (if (= r 39) false (macro? r))))
213+
214+(defn- boundary? [r] (if (whitespace? r) true (terminating? r)))

216+;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
217+;; Tokens (readToken, reader.go:415). The first rune is already consumed and

219+;; byte becomes U+FFFD; a token with none is the input slice.

221+(defn- read-token [st start]

229+ (let [b (buf-new)]

234+ (recur (+ i (bit-and d 7))))))

238+(defn- last-start [st] (- (wasm/get RS 2 st) (wasm/get Aux 2 (aux st))))

980+(defn read-string*
981+ "One form of s starting at rune index `start` (boxed int): a 2-vector
982+ [form end], end the rune index just past what was consumed. Line and
983+ column in error messages count from `start`, as reading (subs s start)
984+ would. Throws, as read-string, when no form is there."
985+ [x start]
986+ (check-string x)
987+ (let [bs (s/str-bytes x) n (wasm/alen bs) want (sq/unbox-int start)
988+ from (loop [i 0 r 0] (if (if (< r want) (< i n) false) (recur (+ i (bit-and (sq/decode-at bs i n) 7)) (inc r)) i))
989+ st (st-new bs from)
990+ v (read-skip st)]
991+ (pv/vconj (pv/vconj (pv/empty-vec) v) (sq/box-int (+ want (wasm/get RS 3 st))))))

1+;; wasm.seq — P2.5 runtime half: let-go's sequence machinery (List,
2+;; EmptyList, Cons, LazySeq, ArrayChunk/ChunkBuffer/ChunkedCons, Range,
3+;; InfiniteRange, Repeat, Reduced, the seq view of a wasm.pvec vector) and the
4+;; Go-native seq fns over them, written in the runtime dialect of pvec.lg:
5+;; IR special forms, IR-op core fns on :int, macros expanding to those, this
6+;; file's own fns, wasm.pvec, and wasm.intrinsics. Ground truth is let-go
7+;; 4e769212 (pkg/vm/*.go, pkg/rt/lang.go, pkg/rt/native_prims.go); SEQ.md
8+;; has the kind table and the realisation/chunking rules with citations.
9+;;
10+;; Calling convention: every public native takes and returns values (refs),
11+;; as a compiled call site passes them; ints arrive boxed and booleans come
12+;; back as Bool refs. `kind` is the ONLY place that type-tests a value; every
13+;; generic fn branches on its result. Errors let-go raises as catchable
14+;; exceptions are raised as D68's Err with let-go's exact message (P2.13,
15+;; D74); wasm/trap is kept for invariant violations and `lower-wasm:` limits.
16+(ns wasm.seq
17+ (:refer-clojure :exclude [list seq first next rest cons count nth peek pop conj
18+ reduce reduced reduced? ensure-reduced unreduced second last
19+ some vec range repeat hash realized? chunk chunk-append
20+ chunk-buffer chunk-cons chunk-first chunk-rest chunk-next
21+ chunked-seq? lazy-seq* map*])
22+ (:require [wasm.intrinsics :as wasm]
23+ [wasm.pvec :as pv]))

25+;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
26+;; The value model (D38), in one place so `kind` sees every box. All runtime
27+;; types share one rec group (D25). Ints are D41's hybrid: i31 when they fit
28+;; 31 bits signed, else an Int box (canonical, so equality may rely on it).
29+(wasm/defstruct Int [:i64])
30+(wasm/defstruct Bool [:i64]) ; 1 true, 0 false
31+(wasm/defstruct Str [:ref [:mut :i64]]) ; UTF-8 bytes, cached hash (-1 = not computed)
32+(wasm/defstruct Char [:i32]) ; rune; any value 0..0x10FFFF, surrogates included (lang.go:6665)
33+(wasm/defstruct Kw [:ref :ref :i64]) ; ns bytes or null, name bytes, hash; interned by wasm.str
34+(wasm/defstruct Sym [:ref :ref :i64]) ; same layout, symbol hash; interned by wasm.str
35+(wasm/defstruct Float [:f64])
36+;; A closure, D52's $Fn exactly: code refs for arities 0/1/2 (null when the
37+;; fn lacks that arity), env, code refs for arities 3/4, and the FnInfo
38+;; (kind, arity, name bytes or null) native's error messages need. Code
39+;; takes the closure itself first, so it reads its captures from field 3.
40+;; invoke0/1/2 are the only call sites here.
41+(wasm/deffunc Code0 [:ref] :ref)
42+(wasm/deffunc Code1 [:ref :ref] :ref)
43+(wasm/deffunc Code2 [:ref :ref :ref] :ref)
44+(wasm/deffunc Code3 [:ref :ref :ref :ref] :ref)
45+(wasm/deffunc Code4 [:ref :ref :ref :ref :ref] :ref)
46+(wasm/defstruct FnInfo [:i32 :i32 :ref])
47+(wasm/defstruct Fn [:funcref :funcref :funcref :ref :funcref :funcref :ref])
48+(wasm/defstruct Env2 [:ref :ref])
49+
50+;; Seq kinds (field order follows the Go structs).
51+(wasm/defstruct List [:ref :ref :i64 :ref]) ; first, next, count, meta; count 0 = EmptyList (list.go:41)
52+(wasm/defstruct Cons [:ref :ref]) ; first, more (a seq, or null) (cons.go:12)
53+(wasm/defstruct LazySeq [[:mut :ref] [:mut :ref] [:mut :i64] [:mut :ref]]) ; fn, realised seq s, done, err (lazy_seq.go:16)
54+(wasm/defstruct ArrayChunk [:ref :i64 :i64]) ; arr (pv/Node), off, end (chunk.go:39)
55+(wasm/defstruct ChunkBuffer [[:mut :ref] [:mut :i64]]) ; arr, n (chunk.go:225)
56+(wasm/defstruct ChunkedCons [:ref :ref]) ; chunk, more (chunk.go:112)
57+(wasm/defstruct Range [:i64 :i64 :i64]) ; start, end, step (range.go:28)
58+(wasm/defstruct InfiniteRange [:i64 :i64]) ; start, step (range.go:156)
59+(wasm/defstruct Repeat [:i64 :ref]) ; i (-1 = infinite), val (repeat.go:22)
60+;; The seq view of a vector. Of a PersistentVector it is PersistentVectorSeq
61+;; (persistent_vector.go:183): 32-wide leaf chunks, prints and hashes as
62+;; "(seq [whole vector])", type Sequence. Of an ArrayVector it is
63+;; ArrayVectorSeq (vector.go:198): chunks of 1, 2, 4, ... (clen, 0 = 1),
64+;; prints "(e_i ...)" from i, type PersistentList (D73).
65+(wasm/defstruct PVecSeq [:ref :i64 :i64]) ; vec, i, clen
66+(wasm/defstruct Reduced [:ref]) ; (reduced.go:6)
67+;; P2.7 boxes. A MapEntry is its own Go type (persistent_map.go:56): Type()
68+;; says ArrayVector and it equals/hashes as the 2-vector, but it is also a
69+;; Seq, key/val accept only it, peek/assoc/subvec refuse it, and with-meta
70+;; returns it unchanged. Atom and Volatile are the backend's $Atom shape
71+;; (one mutable slot; validators and watches are named limits, wasm.core).
72+;; Err is the backend's $Err (kind 0 ex-info, 1 raw runtime error, 2 caught
73+;; runtime error; message bytes; message once caught; ex-data) plus a cause.
74+(wasm/defstruct MapEntry [:ref :ref]) ; key, val
75+(wasm/defstruct Atom [[:mut :ref]])
76+(wasm/defstruct Volatile [[:mut :ref]])
77+(wasm/defstruct Err [:i32 :ref :ref :ref :ref]) ; kind, msg bytes, caught msg bytes, data, cause
78+;; Foreign-kind hooks (kind 18: maps from phm, sets from phs, anything else),
79+;; one Handler per slot so registrations never overwrite each other's:
80+;; slot 0 maps, 1 sets, 2 the generic fallback. A Handler is [pred seq count
81+;; equiv hash], each a Fn; pred (null = matches every foreign value) answers
82+;; whether the value is this handler's. Dispatch tries 0, 1, then 2.
83+(wasm/defstruct Handler [:ref :ref :ref :ref :ref])
84+(wasm/defstruct Hooks [[:mut :ref] [:mut :ref] [:mut :ref] [:mut :ref] [:mut :ref] [:mut :ref] [:mut :ref]]) ; slots 0-2, the printer, seqable?, ifn, type namer
85+(def hooks (wasm/new Hooks (wasm/null) (wasm/null) (wasm/null) (wasm/null) (wasm/null) (wasm/null) (wasm/null)))
86+;; P2.13 (R5, D105): the seq of a map, a set or a transient map is MapSeq or
87+;; SetSeq (map.go:110, set.go:131): a cached array of entries (MapEntry) or
88+;; keys plus an index. Type() is ListType and = is sequential, but neither has
89+;; Hash(), so it hashes by FNV of String() like Range; Conj panics (a recovered
90+;; interface-conversion error), so it is its own kind, not a Cons chain.
91+;; Declared after Hooks so no earlier struct moves in the rec group.
92+(wasm/defstruct ArrSeq [:ref :i64 :i32]) ; arr (pv/Node, never empty), i, flavour (0 MapSeq, 1 SetSeq)
93+
94+(defn box-int [n]
95+ (if (if (>= n -1073741824) (<= n 1073741823) false) (wasm/i31 n) (wasm/new Int n)))
96+(defn unbox-int [x] (if (wasm/i31? x) (wasm/i31-get x) (wasm/get Int 0 x)))
97+(defn bool [b] (wasm/new Bool (if b 1 0)))
98+
99+;; D68 raises. A message that names a type (Go's Type().Name()) gets it from
100+;; the type namer wasm.core installs (slot 6): seq.lg cannot require it.
101+(defn- err-b [bs] (wasm/new Err 1 bs bs (wasm/null) (wasm/null)))
102+(defn- raise-b [bs] (throw (err-b bs)))
103+(defn bytes-cat "a ++ b, fresh Bytes." [a b]
104+ (let [na (wasm/alen a) nb (wasm/alen b) out (wasm/bytes-new (+ na nb))]
105+ (wasm/array-copy wasm/Bytes out 0 a 0 na)
106+ (wasm/array-copy wasm/Bytes out na b 0 nb)
107+ out))
108+(defn set-type-name-hook!
109+ "Install the Fn (f x) -> Str naming x's type as let-go's Type() does
110+ (wasm.core's type-name), for messages that embed a type."
111+ [f] (wasm/set! Hooks 6 hooks f))
112+(declare invoke1)
113+(declare kind-type-name kind)
114+(defn type-name-bytes
115+ "x's let-go type name as bytes: seq.lg names its own kinds; a foreign value
116+ (maps, sets, transients, types...) goes through wasm.core's namer, or reads
117+ let-go.lang.Unknown before wasm.core/install!."
118+ [x]
119+ (let [h (wasm/get Hooks 6 hooks)]
120+ (if (if (= 18 (kind x)) (wasm/null? h) true) (kind-type-name x) (wasm/get Str 0 (invoke1 h x)))))
121+(defn raise-typed "Raise prefix-bytes ++ x's type name (D68)." [prefix x]
122+ (raise-b (bytes-cat prefix (type-name-bytes x))))
123+
124+;; A non-Fn callable (keyword, symbol, map, set, vector: vm.AsFn) is called
125+;; through the ifn hook wasm.core installs (slot 5: code 1 = callable?, code
126+;; 4 = invoke with the argument count); seq.lg cannot require wasm.core. The
127+;; backend lowers calls to these three as its own $rt_invokeN, which does the
128+;; same and also raises native's arity error for a missing arity.
129+(declare kind)
130+(defn- invoke-ifn* [f n a b]
131+ (let [h (wasm/get Hooks 5 hooks)]
132+ (if (wasm/null? h)
133+ (wasm/trap "wasm.seq: a non-Fn callable and no ifn hook installed (wasm.core not linked)")
134+ (wasm/call-ref Code4 (wasm/get Fn 5 h) h f (box-int n) a b))))
135+(defn invoke0 [f] (if (= 16 (kind f)) (wasm/call-ref Code0 (wasm/get Fn 0 f) f) (invoke-ifn* f 0 (wasm/null) (wasm/null))))
136+(defn invoke1 [f a] (if (= 16 (kind f)) (wasm/call-ref Code1 (wasm/get Fn 1 f) f a) (invoke-ifn* f 1 a (wasm/null))))
137+(defn invoke2 [f a b] (if (= 16 (kind f)) (wasm/call-ref Code2 (wasm/get Fn 2 f) f a b) (invoke-ifn* f 2 a b)))
138+
139+(defn mk-fn1 "A closure with only arity 1 (hook code)." [code]
140+ (wasm/new Fn (wasm/null) code (wasm/null) (wasm/null) (wasm/null) (wasm/null) (wasm/null)))
141+(defn mk-fn2 "A closure with only arity 2 (hook code)." [code]
142+ (wasm/new Fn (wasm/null) (wasm/null) code (wasm/null) (wasm/null) (wasm/null) (wasm/null)))
143+
144+(defn set-kind-hooks!
145+ "Register the Handler for one slot (:int 0 maps, 1 sets, 2 generic): pred
146+ (or null), seq, count, equiv, hash, each a Fn. Null seq-fn clears the slot."
147+ [slot pred seq-fn count-fn equiv-fn hash-fn]
148+ (let [h (if (wasm/null? seq-fn) (wasm/null) (wasm/new Handler pred seq-fn count-fn equiv-fn hash-fn))]
149+ (cond (= slot 0) (wasm/set! Hooks 0 hooks h)
150+ (= slot 1) (wasm/set! Hooks 1 hooks h)
151+ :else (wasm/set! Hooks 2 hooks h))))
152+
153+(defn set-hooks!
154+ "The generic fallback slot (2), matching every foreign value no other slot
155+ claims. All nulls clear it."
156+ [seq-fn count-fn equiv-fn hash-fn]
157+ (set-kind-hooks! 2 (wasm/null) seq-fn count-fn equiv-fn hash-fn))
158+
159+(defn set-print-hook!
160+ "Install the printer that hashing non-int Range/Repeat/PVecSeq elements
161+ needs (Go hashes those kinds by FNV over String()): a Fn called as (f x)
162+ returning a Str of x's readable form. wasm.core's install! passes
163+ wasm.str's pr-str; seq.lg cannot require wasm.str."
164+ [f] (wasm/set! Hooks 3 hooks f))
165+
166+(defn set-ifn-hook!
167+ "Install the Fn wasm.core links non-Fn callables through: code 1 (f x) ->
168+ Bool, is x callable (vm.AsFn); code 4 (f x n a b) -> x called with n
169+ (0-2) of a b."
170+ [f] (wasm/set! Hooks 5 hooks f))
171+
172+(declare truthy?)
173+(defn callable?
174+ "vm.AsFn: a Fn, or a value the ifn hook says calls itself."
175+ [f]
176+ (if (= 16 (kind f))
177+ true
178+ (let [h (wasm/get Hooks 5 hooks)]
179+ (if (wasm/null? h) false (truthy? (wasm/call-ref Code1 (wasm/get Fn 1 h) h f))))))
180+
181+(defn set-seqable-hook!
182+ "Install the Fn (f x) -> Bool saying whether a foreign value is seqable
183+ natively (a map, a set, a transient map), so first/rest/seq/reduce & co.
184+ raise their own let-go message for the others (a type value, a transient
185+ set or vector, a meta'd keyword). Null: every foreign value is seqable."
186+ [f] (wasm/set! Hooks 4 hooks f))
187+
188+(declare truthy?)
189+
190+(defn- claims? [h x]
191+ (if (wasm/null? h)
192+ false
193+ (let [p (wasm/get Handler 0 h)] (if (wasm/null? p) true (truthy? (invoke1 p x))))))
194+
195+(defn- hook
196+ "Hook i (1 seq, 2 count, 3 equiv, 4 hash) of the Handler that claims x."
197+ [i x]
198+ (let [h0 (wasm/get Hooks 0 hooks)
199+ h (if (claims? h0 x)
200+ h0
201+ (let [h1 (wasm/get Hooks 1 hooks)]
202+ (if (claims? h1 x)
203+ h1
204+ (let [h2 (wasm/get Hooks 2 hooks)]
205+ (if (claims? h2 x) h2 (wasm/trap "wasm.seq: foreign value and no hook installed (phm/phs not linked)"))))))]
206+ (cond (= i 1) (wasm/get Handler 1 h) (= i 2) (wasm/get Handler 2 h)
207+ (= i 3) (wasm/get Handler 3 h) :else (wasm/get Handler 4 h))))
